analysis.title: Are We There Yet
key_insights: The SOX has posted two consecutive up days and Asia is also higher after weeks of tech weakness. The note asks whether the worst is over. Positioning has been flushed in some places but remains crowded in others.
Goldman Prime data show fundamental long/short momentum exposure falling from nearly 70% at the peak to around 15%.
Asian fundamental long/short managers cut net leverage by 16.9 percentage points to 48%, the 21st percentile over the past year.

King Callahan (GS) describes the semis move as one of the more dynamic and painful stretches he can remember. Earnings and capex estimates keep rising, valuations are cheaper and positioning is cleaner, yet investors are reluctant to step back in.

Callahan says the SOX trades at about a 1x discount to its 15-year average multiple. He does not think sentiment has turned outright bearish. Buyers are waiting for the market to reward estimate revisions rather than compress multiples on peak-cycle concerns.
The S&P 500 excluding AI is retreating after testing its highs, while the Nasdaq 100 is bouncing from the bottom of its summer range.
Nasdaq futures length remains elevated heading into MegaCap earnings, despite the momentum unwind.

CTA Nasdaq trend signals have weakened considerably and short-term momentum is under pressure. A rebound would help repair the technical picture, while another leg lower risks more systematic selling.
The note's summary is that tech fundamentals are strong and improving, positioning is still messy, and systematic flows do not respond to fundamentals.
